## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.

The proxy side is sibling llm item **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** ("Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes availability"), which has **not shipped**: probed 2026-11-10 against the live proxy (`http://192.168.0.199:8000`) — `/openapi.json` lists `/llama/local/status` and `/llama/local/reserve` only, and `/llama/local/audit`, `/llama/local/budget`, `/llama/local/audit/status` all answer `404`.

So this child **pins the client-side contract before the server exists**, exactly as the reserve-handshake slice C1 did (`downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts` header: types + tolerant parser first, client second, "NOTHING here is called on the dispatch path yet").

## Scope

Provisional wire contract (one constant, one parser, no behaviour change):

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH = '/llama/local/audit/status'` in `downtime-worker.constants.ts` (documented as provisional; the proxy's final path is a one-line change).
- `AuditAvailability` type: `{ cap: number; live: number; available: boolean; leases?: AuditAvailabilityLease[]; reclaimed?: number }` plus the refusal-reason token the proxy uses.
- `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse(raw, httpStatus): AuditAvailability | null` — fail-closed tolerant parse with alias accessors for the fields whose names are not yet fixed (`cap|max|max_audit`, `live|in_flight|live_leases`, `available|can_admit`), lease entries carrying an expiry, and `null` for every unusable payload (never a permissive default).
- Tests: table-driven fixtures pinning grant / saturated / malformed / alias spellings / absent lease array / negative or non-finite numbers / non-object bodies.
- Documentation of the provisional contract and the 2026-11-10 probe result in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

No production call site consumes the parser in this child (no behaviour change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`, the `AuditAvailability` (and lease) types and `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse` exist in a new module `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`, exported from the barrel only where the later children need them.
- The parser maps a valid payload to `{ cap, live, available, leases? }`, taking `available` from the proxy's own field and never deriving a permissive value from missing data.
- Alias tolerance is pinned: each documented alias spelling parses to the same typed result, and an unrecognised-but-valid extra field is ignored (additive evolution).
- Malformed input (non-object, missing/non-finite/negative `cap` or `live`, `leases` not an array) returns `null` — a garbage payload can never be read as "available".
- A table-driven test file pins every case, and no production dispatch path imports the parser yet (asserted by a test).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records the provisional contract, that the proxy side is LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK, and the 2026-11-10 probe result (endpoint absent on the live proxy).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

1. Add the constants + types + pure parser module (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`).
2. Add the table-driven contract test (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`).
3. Add the barrel re-export following the existing `downtime-worker.local-reservation.contract.ts` pattern.

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`


## Impact

Operators can stop worrying that a malformed or legacy proxy response will be misread as audit capacity: every payload the future audit gate cannot trust is rejected outright, and a field or path rename on either side stays a one-line change.

# Add the fail-closed audit-availability client

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisite: the pinned wire contract (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`).

The counterpart of `createLocalReserver` (`downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`) and `createDowntimePoller` (`downtime-worker.poller.ts`): one bounded GET of the proxy's audit availability, with the failure classification **spelled out as a typed outcome** so the dispatcher's policy (fail closed, named reason) never has to guess from an empty value.

## Scope

`createAuditAvailabilityClient(proxyUrl, fetcher = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS)` returning a client that resolves one typed outcome per call:

- `{ status: 'ok', availability }` — 2xx with a parseable payload.
- `{ status: 'endpoint-absent', reason: 'http-404' }` — the proxy predates the endpoint (the sibling item has not shipped).
- `{ status: 'unreachable', reason: 'timeout' | 'network' | 'http-<status>' }` — the proxy could not be reached or answered an unusable status.
- `{ status: 'unparsable', reason: 'bad-body' }` — 2xx with a body the pinned parser rejects.

The client never throws; the URL is normalised with the same trailing-slash convention as the reserve client; the abort timer is always cleared.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createAuditAvailabilityClient` exists in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts` and resolves exactly the four typed outcomes above, never throwing.
- `GET` is used, the URL is `{proxyUrl}{AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH}` with a normalised trailing slash, and the request is bounded by the timeout (abort is asserted in a test).
- `404` classifies as `endpoint-absent`; a `5xx`, a non-JSON body, a network rejection and an abort all classify as `unreachable`/`unparsable` with the reason naming the failing exchange.
- A 2xx payload the parser rejects is `unparsable` — never `ok` with partial data.
- Tests inject a fake fetcher and cover every outcome, the URL normalisation, the method/header, and the timer cleanup (no open handle after the call).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Implement the client in `downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts` (reuse `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS`).
2. Add the injected-fetcher test file following `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`.
3. Re-export from the barrel where the dispatcher deps are wired.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the availability read is cheap enough to call once per audit candidate per tick (the current `readAuditBudgetState` pre-check is a local file read; the proxy read adds one local-network GET). If tick cost becomes a problem, a short-lived cache is a follow-up item, not scope here.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`

## Impact

Operators can now tell, in one typed outcome, whether the proxy refused an audit because the budget is full, whether it has not shipped the endpoint yet, or whether the proxy is unreachable or answering garbage — so a fail-closed audit hold names the real cause instead of looking like an empty value.

# Audit gate reads proxy availability

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisites: the pinned contract and the availability client.

Today `getActiveAudit` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) consults `readAuditBudgetState` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`), which reads the **per-host** `~/.herdr/downtime/budget.json` `maxAudit` cap plus the machine-scoped `dispatch-budget.json` ledger. Two ContextHub hosts therefore each believe they are under cap while both contend for the single local `llama-server` GPU — the 2026-11-03 incident.

This child makes the **audit tier only** proxy-derived; the implement tier is untouched.

## Scope

- Inject the availability read into the worker deps (`readAuditAvailability` seam on `DowntimeWorkerDeps`), wired in `main()` as `createAuditAvailabilityClient(runSettings.downtimeProxyUrl)` — the same wiring point as `reserveLocalCapacity`.
- `getActiveAudit` audit tier: query the proxy availability and map it to the result — `available === false` → `{ ok: true, active: true, source: 'proxy', reason: 'audit-budget-saturated', budget: { live, max: cap } }`; `available === true` → `{ ok: true, active: false, source: 'proxy' }`.
- The audit tier no longer asserts `budget.json` `maxAudit`; `readAuditBudgetState` is not called on the proxy path.
- Typed result changes in `downtime-worker.types.ts`: `source` gains `'proxy'`, `reason` gains `'audit-budget-saturated'` and `'audit-budget-unknown'`; the proxy's own token vocabulary is reused verbatim (one spelling shared with the proxy, no local renaming).
- Fail-closed mapping (AC3): `endpoint-absent` / `unreachable` / `unparsable` → `{ ok: true, active: true, source: 'proxy', reason: 'audit-budget-unknown' }` with the proxy error detail carried for the decision log — audit dispatch stops, with a named reason, instead of silently reverting to the per-host cap.
- The per-worklog dispatch-marker single-flight check below the host-wide check is retained unchanged (it answers a different question: "has this worklog already been audited this window").

## Acceptance Criteria

- For the audit tier, `getActiveAudit` returns `source: 'proxy'` with the proxy's verdict and evidence, and a test proves `budget.json` `maxAudit` (any value, including `0`) does not influence the proxy-path decision.
- A proxy `available: false` verdict yields `active: true, reason: 'audit-budget-saturated'` carrying the proxy's `live`/`cap` as `budget` evidence.
- An unreachable/absent/unparsable proxy yields `active: true, reason: 'audit-budget-unknown'` with the failing exchange recorded (timeout / network / http-404 / bad-body) — never a permissive `active: false`.
- The audit-path refusal tokens are defined once (`audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown`) with a literal-value test shared with the proxy's vocabulary, and the proxy path no longer produces the legacy `host-budget-audit` / `audit-host-saturated` tokens (asserted by a test).
- The implement tier is provably unchanged: `admitHostDispatch` still refuses/permits on `budget.json` `maxImplement` and the local ledger, and its existing tests pass unmodified.
- The availability read is invoked once per audit gate evaluation (a test counts the calls), and the deps seam is optional so every existing test double keeps compiling (a missing seam fails closed as `audit-budget-unknown`, not open).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC1 — Audit admission is proxy-derived.** For the audit tier only, `getActiveAudit` / the dispatch gate queries the proxy's audit-availability endpoint (cap, live leases, available) and does not assert the local `budget.json` cap. The implement tier keeps its existing per-host budget (out of scope).
- **AC2 — One vocabulary, no disagreement.** The refusal reason token and log vocabulary match the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`), so a dispatcher admission and a proxy refusal cannot disagree; a divergence is logged with both sides' evidence.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the `readAuditAvailability` seam to `DowntimeWorkerDeps` (+ the barrel wiring in `main()`).
2. Extend `DowntimeActiveAuditResult` (`source: 'proxy'`, the two new reason tokens) and the decision-log vocabulary constants.
3. Rewrite the host-wide branch of `getActiveAudit` to consume the seam and map outcomes (fail closed on every non-`ok` outcome).
4. Export/propagate the token so `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` reports it as today's `audit-host-saturated` is reported.
5. Add scenario tests to `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` and the seam-wiring test in `index.downtime-select.test.ts`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the proxy read adds one local GET per audit gate evaluation. Mitigated by the fact that the gate is already evaluated once per tick.
- **Risk (accepted by design, parent AC3):** a proxy outage stops audit dispatch. The named reason and the operator-visible log are the mitigation; the one-release legacy escape hatch is the next child.
- **Assumption:** the proxy's `available` verdict is authoritative even when the dispatcher's local ledger disagrees — the local ledger becomes observability-only (reconciled in the next child's divergence log).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-budget.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-select.test.ts`

## Impact

An audit is now admitted by the shared proxy's live capacity, so two ContextHub hosts can no longer each believe they are under their own per-host cap and overload the single local GPU.

# Admission choke point, divergence log and legacy flag

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisite: the audit gate reads proxy availability.

`admitHostDispatch` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`) is the single admission reader both dispatcher paths funnel through once per dispatch attempt. Its header promises that "a refusal before selection and a refusal at admission agree" — so the audit branch must reach the same proxy-derived decision, not the local `maxAudit` cap.

## Scope

- `admitHostDispatch` audit branch: delegate to the proxy-derived decision (reuse `readAuditBudgetState`'s replacement from the previous child), so the pre-check and admission cannot disagree. Refusal tokens are the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown`).
- Local ledger stays as **observability only** for the audit tier: the dispatch still reserves / confirms / releases its audit entry (so the worklist header, the interactive dialog, the closed-pane sweep and the release paths keep working unchanged), but the entry is never read to refuse an audit. Document that in the module header.
- Divergence log (AC2): when the proxy admits but the local fresh audit count is at/over `maxAudit`, or the proxy refuses while the local count is below the cap, write one decision-log entry naming both sides' evidence (`proxy: {live, cap, available}` vs `local: {live, maxAudit}`). No divergence → no entry (no log noise).
- One-release legacy escape hatch (AC3): env flag `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` restores the pre-change behaviour (per-host `budget.json` `maxAudit` + local ledger) for the audit tier; read per tick, documented as one-release, with a removal note.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch({kind:'audit'})` refuses and admits on the proxy verdict only; a test drives both a permissive `budget.json` and a permissive proxy, then a saturated proxy, and proves the proxy decides.
- The pre-check and admission agree: a test pins that the same availability state yields the same admission answer through `getActiveAudit` and `admitHostDispatch`, and that the refusal token is identical on both sides (AC2).
- A divergence (proxy admits / local ledger at cap, and the inverse) writes exactly one decision-log entry carrying both sides' evidence; an agreeing state writes none.
- With `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` the audit tier returns to the `budget.json` + local-ledger decision (existing `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` semantics), the proxy is not consulted, and a warning marks the legacy path in the log.
- The implement tier's admission and reservation behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing tests pass unmodified; one new pin asserts the implement branch never reads the proxy).
- Audit entries are still reserved, confirmed and released locally (a test asserts the ledger entry lifecycle on both the admit and refuse paths), and the audit entry alone can never cause a refusal.
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe on an unreachable proxy.** If the proxy cannot be reached, audit dispatch fails **closed** with a named reason (e.g. `audit-budget-unknown`) and logs the proxy error; the legacy local-ledger path remains behind an explicit flag for one release.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Replace the audit branch of `admitHostDispatch` with the proxy-derived decision + reservation-for-observability.
2. Add the divergence comparison and decision-log entry (`downtime-log-budget.ts` vocabulary).
3. Add the `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET` flag reader + legacy branch.
4. Extend `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` and `host-dispatch-budget.machine.test.ts` with the agreement/divergence/flag cases.

Operators can trust that an audit is admitted by the shared proxy's live capacity — two ContextHub hosts can no longer each believe they are under their own per-host cap — with any proxy/local disagreement recorded alongside both sides' evidence, and a one-release flag to fall back to the old local decision.

# Cross-host audit serialisation acceptance proof

## Context

Parent: **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.

The incident this parent exists to fix: two ContextHub hosts, each enforcing its own `maxAudit: 1`, produced two concurrent audits on the single local GPU (2026-11-03). Per-host unit tests cannot prove that is now impossible; a scenario with **two dispatcher instances sharing one stub proxy** can.

## Scope

An integration-level acceptance suite (`packages/herdr/src/audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts`) that runs two dispatcher admission paths against one in-process stub proxy implementing the pinned availability contract:

1. Host A is admitted (proxy `available: true`), the stub proxy then reports the live lease (`available: false`) — host B is refused with `audit-budget-saturated`.
2. Both hosts are refused with the same token and the same evidence (dispatcher and proxy agree) — the AC2 agreement at the cross-host level, not just per call.
3. The proxy is unreachable (stub closed) — both hosts fail closed with `audit-budget-unknown` and no pane spawn.
4. Stale-lease reclamation: the stub reports one lease already expired plus `available: true` — host B dispatches; the read reflects the proxy's reclamation rather than holding a phantom slot.
5. The implement tier on both hosts is unaffected by the stub's audit state (proxy switching from available to saturated changes no implement admission answer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The suite drives two independent dispatcher instances through one stub proxy and asserts per-case: admission answer, refusal token, evidence and whether a spawn happened.
- Case 1 fails on the pre-change code (a regression pin: with per-host caps both hosts admit) and passes after the parent's change — the test documents the incident it prevents.
- Case 2 asserts the dispatcher's token equals the stub proxy's refusal reason string (`audit-budget-saturated`), proving one vocabulary.
- Case 3 asserts `audit-budget-unknown` on both hosts, no spawn, and the proxy error recorded in the decision log.
- Case 4 asserts dispatch proceeds when only expired leases are reported (reclamation reflected), with the lease evidence in the log.
- Case 5 asserts the implement tier's admission answers are identical before and after the stub's audit verdict changes.
- The suite needs no network access (the stub is in-process) and leaves no open handles.
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: availability read maps to the dispatch decision; second audit refused with agreement between dispatcher and proxy; unreachable proxy fails closed; stale-lease reclamation reflected; the implement tier is unchanged. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Build the in-process stub proxy (an injected `fetcher` or a `node:http` server on port 0) implementing the pinned availability contract.
2. Wire two dispatch-gate instances through `createDowntimeDeps`-style seams with the stub as `readAuditAvailability`.
3. Cover the five scenarios with decision-log assertions.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the stub is the contract record — if the proxy's real shape differs, the stub and the pinned parser change together (one path constant + aliases), not the scenarios.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`

## Impact

Operators can now point to a single cross-host acceptance proof that two ContextHub hosts can no longer dispatch concurrent audits on the shared local GPU: once one host's audit lease is live, the second host is refused with the proxy's own `audit-budget-saturated` token, and an unreachable proxy stops audits on every host instead of silently falling back to per-host caps.

# herdr worklist: substituted critical-child root loses `childCount`, so the parent cannot be expanded and the critical child is unreachable

## Goal

A critical **child** work item whose root ancestor is pulled into the worklist by
critical-child root substitution must be reachable in the herdr Work Items pane:
the substituted root row must render an expand arrow and expand to show its
children, exactly as it does when the same root arrives from the browse feed.

## Problem

Observed 2026-11-12 in the live Work Items pane (`wD:p180`, worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`):

```
    ⭐  🔓📋✅   LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS Serialise audits at the shared local resource… [plan_complete] ⭐ high
```

Two leading spaces where every expandable row renders `▶`/`▼`:

```
  ▶ ⭐  ⛔📋❌   LP-0MW7V14DN007F127 …
```

`LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (**Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes
availability**, `critical`, `open`, `intake_complete`) is a child of
`LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS`. The top level only renders root items
(`selectWorkItems`, `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` rootOnly gate), so
the child is only reachable by expanding its parent — and the parent cannot be
expanded, so the child never appears.

**Root cause.** `substituteCriticalRoots`
(`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) resolves a critical child's
ancestors through the in-process DB fast path (`db.get`) or the `wl show`
fallback (`fetchItemDetails`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts:306`). Neither
emits `childCount`; only the enrichments in `wl list` / `wl next` /
`wl worklist` do (e.g. the child read at `fetcher.api.ts:517`). With
`childCount === undefined` every expand path is gated off:

- `worklist.ts:271` — the arrow renders only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:1601` — `Tab` toggles only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:5329` — that `Tab` path is the only on-demand
  `fetchChildrenForItem` entry, so children are never even fetched.

**Reproduction** with the plugin's own source (no mocks), worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`:

```
root via substitution: present cc=undefined
critical child at top level: false
```

i.e. `mergeMandatoryAndSelect(browseWithoutRoot, allMandatory, 25,
fetchItemDetails)` returns the root with `childCount === undefined`. The same
root fetched normally carries `childCount: 9`.

**Trigger condition.** When the root does not win one of the `browseItemCount`
"other" slots (in the observed case `othersLimit = 0`: 24–25 mandatory rows in
a 25-item window), `mergeUniqueById(enrichedItems, substituted.mandatory)` has
no enriched copy to keep, and `ensureSubstitutedRoots` restores the substituted
(childCount-less) object. Whenever the root is *in* the browse window the
enriched copy wins and the arrow is correct — so the defect is window-pressure
dependent.

**Impact beyond display.** `getHerdrListHead` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:527`)
feeds the downtime dispatcher the same `fetchNextItems` output. The list head
therefore offers the substituted root (here: no `risk`/`effort` → a
`risk-effort` dispatch) and never the release-blocking critical child, so the
child is invisible to both the operator and auto-dispatch. The data layer is
otherwise sound: `wl next -n 25` ranks the child #1 and
`wl show LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS --children --json` returns it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Substituted roots are expandable.** A root injected by
  `substituteCriticalRoots` carries the same `childCount` a browse/`wl list`
  fetch would give it, so `formatItemLine` renders `▶` for it.
- **AC2 — Children are reachable.** With the root substituted (browse feed
  deliberately without it), `Tab`/`Enter` on that row triggers the on-demand
  child fetch and the critical child renders underneath it.
- **AC3 — Regression test for the window-pressure case.** A unit test asserts
  that when `othersLimit === 0` and a critical child's root is only in the
  mandatory set, the returned root has `childCount > 0` and is expandable;
  a second test pins that the browse-sourced root keeps its enriched
  `childCount` (no double-count, no clobber).
- **AC4 — Dispatcher head parity.** A test asserts the Herdr list head
  (`getHerdrListHead` / `fetchNextItems`) exposes the same expandable root
  shape used for rendering, so display and dispatch cannot diverge.
- **AC5 — Docs.** The critical-child root substitution comment block in
  `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` (and the reachability contract note in
  `smart-selection.ts`) records that substituted roots must carry
  `childCount`, and why a stripped ancestor is unsafe.
- **AC6 — Tests.** Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`; the full suite
  passes at the dev-push gate.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — `substituteCriticalRoots`
  / `walkToRootAncestor` ancestor lookups (`db.get`, injected `itemDetails`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` — `fetchItemDetails` (no `childCount`),
  `readChildrenInProcess` (already computes `db.getChildCounts(allRaw)` at
  line ~504 — the reusable source).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand affordances gated on `childCount`
  (lines 271, 1601, 5329).
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — new regression tests (AC3/AC4).

## Out of scope

- The rootOnly top-level rendering rule itself (`selectWorkItems`).
- Any `llm`-side change; this is a `packages/herdr` display/reachability defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `childCount` is the canonical "has children" signal for the
  expand affordance; two independent gates (`worklist.ts:1601`, `5329`) agree.
- **Risk:** counting children at ancestor-resolution time could add cost to a
  refresh. Mitigation: reuse the existing single-connection in-process
  `getChildCounts` pass rather than a per-item spawn, and fall back to leaving
  the arrow absent (today's behaviour) if the read fails — fail-open, never a
  crash.
- **Discovery:** found while investigating why `LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (llm
  worklog) was absent from the herdr Work Items pane.

## Impact

The herdr Work Items pane now renders a substituted critical-child root with an expand arrow even under window pressure, so the critical child is reachable by expanding the root — in both the pane and the downtime dispatcher list head.
